title: Onboarding-to-commitment: Approval SLAs and Post-Provisioning Capacity Reconciliation
creator: Lina Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures the end-to-end flow from a customer reservation request through approval, capacity commit, and the post-provisioning reconciliation step. Goals are to define SLAs for approvals, an escalation matrix for complex requests, the metadata required to size throughput guarantees, and a reconciliation job to validate provisioned vs committed capacity (and flag billing/forecast drift).

Scope:
- Intake form fields and validations for capacity sizing (qps, avg seq len, peak concurrency, burst window, redundancy needs)
- Approval SLAs by tier (self-serve, commercial, enterprise) and corresponding gating checks (security review, budget, hardware constraints)
- Roles and responsibilities for the approvals pipeline (Sales, TPM, Capacity Ops, Infra)
comments: 2026-01-16 - Lina Patel: Initial draft of intake fields added to Confluence. Included estimated delta calculation for token throughput based on seq length. Asking ENG for validation on feasibility of reporting fields (qps vs throughput).

2026-01-19 - Miles Ortega: Reviewed intake form; requested adding 'expected monthly committed hours' and 'preferred regions' to capture capacity constraints. Noted that KV cache requirements can materially change cluster sizing — ENG to add checkbox for 'predictable KV cache retention'.

2026-01-22 - Priya Rao (Infra): Provided feedback on sizing assumptions. For GPU families we need both 'p99 latency target' and 'percent of requests eligible for batching' to choose kernel profiles. Recommended we default to conservative throughput when fields are missing and surface a justification to customer.

2026-01-27 - Lina Patel: Updated approval SLA table. Proposal: self-serve <= 4 hours, commercial (under $X/month) 48 hours, enterprise (with security review) 7 business days. Added escalation path to Capacity Ops Slack channel and on-call rota.

2026-01-31 - Legal (Sara Mills): Noted that enterprise approvals require a mandatory security_review_required flag and that audit log retention requirements must be captured for Private deployments. Added as a gating check.

2026-02-02 - Miles Ortega: Implementation plan drafted. Breaking into three deliverables: 1) Intake UI + validations (PM/Design), 2) Approval workflow + SLA enforcement (Backend + Workflows), 3) Reconciliation job (offline process to compare committed vs provisioned and emit alerts & billing adjustments). Created sub-issues for dev work and linked PRD.
notes:
Trade-offs discussed:
- Fast approvals vs safe capacity allocation: we will allow provisional, time-bound commits (e.g., 72-hour provisional reservations) that can be auto-rescinded if final security/budget checks fail. This reduces time-to-onboard but requires a reconciliation job to reconcile allocations and billing.
- Conservative default sizing when inputs missing will reduce outage risk but may increase cost for customers; the reconciliation job will propose credits if actual usage is below commit thresholds.

Open questions:
- Exact billing credit formula for over-provisioned capacity (Finance to propose).
- How to expose provisional window limits in the Console UI and API (Design + SDK).

Next steps:
- ENG to validate the minimum set of telemetry required to power the reconciliation job (ETA 2026-02-09).
- Design to produce final intake wireframes (ETA 2026-02-05).
- SalesOps to review SLA tiers and pricing impacts (meeting 2026-02-04).

acceptance_criteria: Intake UI with required fields published to Console and API; server-side validation enforced
Approval workflow implemented with SLA timers, escalation routing, and audit logs
Reconciliation job runs daily and produces a report comparing committed capacity vs provisioned capacity with actionable alerts
Billing exceptions pipeline defined for crediting customers when provisioning overshot commitments
Documentation published for Sales/CS and internal runbook for Capacity Ops
